nodes.title: C1 item 6, M3a: the 'zoom' is drawn, not a camera. A camera op (animating the board's viewBox) was planned and rejected before building: an SVG zoom scales text with the drawing, so labels that overlap at full size still overlap zoomed (overlap is scale-invariant) and only legibility changes. number-line-zoom@1 instead draws the textbook magnified segment: the line a..a+3 (4 labels: an axis to W9), the unit [a, a+1] lit, its copy lifts off, stretches (scale about its left end) and lands as the full-width lower line (claim), guide lines below the labels, the lower line labelled in fifths (an axis) with ten tenth ticks and the value marked. pick.js: a decimal to locate/compare/order in a decimal-context kit, never an item's answer (it would be written '?'), never in a line doing arithmetic.
nodes.reversal: a lesson needs to zoom something with no magnified-segment form (a map region, a microscope view): then a camera op judged in its own view

nodes.title: W9 (main): a bare '0' or '1' was skipped as a number-line origin or column label, so a place-value board could show a hidden 0 or 1. A 0/1 that ENDS inside a rect (its settled position: place-value digits rise into their boxes) is now judged like any digit, and the number containing it is masked too. Tested in r7-motion-templates.

md.decisions:
## dc-r7-zoom-in-drawing: zooming into a number line (2026-11-05)

To show where a decimal lies, the board lifts the unit it lies in off the number line and stretches it into a big line split into tenths, as a textbook draws it. Labels stay readable because the drawing is enlarged, not the view.
